brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Three full-depth 3-compartment bins: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (9 compartments total), each dressed with a kitchen utensil prop visible from above.

Two hex-acc-keyhole accessories (accessory:0#-1,0#1 and accessory:0#1,0#1) fitted in the same slot-1 face direction on the two end cells, so the row lifts onto wall screws; caps (capOpenFaces) and joint bolts (lockJoints) applied, check_build ok with meshClash clear.

Open-top divided bins suit spice jars; no spice-jar prop exists in the catalog, so compartments are staged with spoon/fork/knife props to show kitchen storage use. Note: configurator checks fit only, not load rating of the hangers.

finish.summary: A wall-hung spice rack: three full hex cells in a row, each holding a full-depth 3-compartment bin (9 compartments for spice jars), with keyhole hanger accessories on both end cells in the same wall-facing direction, end caps and joint bolts fitted. Check passes with mesh clear; compartments staged with kitchen utensils since no spice-jar props exist.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
